name: JCH Optimize
author: codealfa

sections.description:
Make your WordPress site load faster, score higher on PageSpeed Insights, and pass Core Web Vitals, without editing a line of code.

JCH Optimize optimizes each page as WordPress serves it. It combines and minifies your CSS and JavaScript, inlines the critical CSS so the page paints right away, lazy loads offscreen images, caches whole pages, and more. It targets the metrics Google measures: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), First Contentful Paint (FCP), Total Blocking Time (TBT) and Time to First Byte (TTFB).

It never modifies your theme, your plugins or your files. Deactivate it and your site is exactly as it was.

Why speed matters

  • Visitors stay. Slow pages lose people before they see your content. Fast pages keep them reading, browsing and buying.
  • Better search visibility. Google uses Core Web Vitals as part of its page experience ranking signals.
  • More conversions. Each second you save makes it easier for visitors to sign up, check out or get in touch.

Free features

Page caching

  • Page Cache. Serves pages from the cache without running WordPress for each visit, so the first byte arrives sooner.
  • Browser caching for cached pages, following the cache lifetime you set.
  • Campaign-friendly caching. Ignores ad and social tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, msclkid) so links from campaigns still get the cached page.
  • Leaves personal pages out. Logged-in users and visitors who just submitted a form, such as a WooCommerce cart, aren’t served cached pages.
  • Scheduled cleanup of expired cache, run by WP-Cron instead of slowing down visitors’ page loads.
  • Editors can clear the cache from Tools > Page Cache, without access to the settings.

CSS and JavaScript

  • Automatic Settings. Six levels from Minimum to Optimum set up file optimization for you. Start at Minimum and move up.
  • Combine and minify CSS, JavaScript and HTML to cut file sizes and requests.
  • Optimize CSS Delivery. Extracts the critical CSS for the top of each page, inlines it, and loads the rest without blocking rendering. This addresses PageSpeed’s render-blocking resources warning.
  • Dynamic CSS Selectors. Keeps styles for menus, sliders and other elements that JavaScript adds after the page loads in the critical CSS.
  • Defer JavaScript or move it to the bottom of the page.
  • Remove CSS and JavaScript files your pages don’t need.
  • Custom, mobile and desktop CSS, added after your combined CSS so it takes precedence.
  • Exclusions for files, plugins and pages that need to be left alone.

Images

  • Lazy load images below the first screen, so they load only when the visitor scrolls near them.
  • Add width and height attributes to images that are missing them, preventing layout shifts (CLS).
  • Sprite Generator. Combines small background images into one file.

Delivery

  • GZip compression and browser caching rules written to .htaccess for you.
  • CDN / cookieless domain support to serve static files from another domain.
  • HTTP/2 Preload for JavaScript modules and the files you choose.

Built to be safe

  • Development / Production Mode Switcher in the admin bar: switch optimization off while you work on your site, then back on, with the settings pages still available.
  • Dashboard with an optimization snapshot and notifications, including a warning when another page caching plugin is active.
  • Logs that tell you why a page wasn’t optimized or cached.

Go further with JCH Optimize Pro

The free version gets you a long way. JCH Optimize Pro adds the features that move the hardest PageSpeed metrics (LCP, unused CSS and JavaScript, image delivery), plus tools that tell you how your site performs for real visitors.

  • AI-Assisted Optimization (beta). An AI optimizes a page of your site the way an experienced person would. It tries each batch of settings on a private preview your visitors don’t see, checks in a browser for anything that broke and fixes it, and measures the result with PageSpeed Insights on mobile and desktop. It keeps the settings that made the page faster and ends with a report of the scores before and after. Needs an AI Optimization license and your own Anthropic (Claude) or OpenAI API key.
  • Page Experience (real-user monitoring). Measures LCP, INP, CLS, FCP and TTFB in your visitors’ own browsers and charts them day by day, by device and by page. Set a baseline and get an email when your site gets slower.
  • Optimize Images. Compresses images and creates WebP and AVIF versions and responsive sizes for phones and tablets, then serves them automatically. Scheduled optimization works through new images in the background, and your originals are always kept.
  • LCP image preloading. Finds the image that real visitors’ browsers report as each page’s largest paint and loads it first, on mobile and desktop.
  • Reduce unused CSS and JavaScript. Holds back CSS and scripts until the visitor interacts with the page, and loads analytics and ad scripts after the first paint, so they don’t count against your LCP or TBT.
  • Optimize Fonts. Hosts Google Fonts on your own site, preloads the fonts the top of the page needs, and adds size-matched fallback fonts so text doesn’t jump when web fonts load.
  • Advanced lazy loading for iframes, CSS background images, audio and video, plus a lightweight placeholder that stands in for YouTube embeds until clicked.
  • Reduce DOM size by loading chosen sections of the page after it renders.
  • Faster, smarter caching. Serve cached pages as static files straight from the web server, store the cache in Redis, Memcached or APCu, warm the cache with the Recache crawler, and purge the right pages automatically when you publish or update content. Other systems can purge pages through the REST API.
  • Cloudflare integration. Purges Cloudflare’s copies of your pages along with JCH Optimize’s, and switches Cloudflare’s Development Mode with the Mode Switcher.
  • Multiple CDN domains and Smart Combine bundling for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.
  • Ticket support. Open a private support ticket for bugs in JCH Optimize and for anything it breaks on your site, such as a menu, a slider or a form, whether the settings came from an AI-assisted run or were set by hand.

Get started in minutes

  1. Install and activate JCH Optimize.
  2. While you configure it, switch off other page caching plugins.
  3. Go to Settings > JCH Optimize and choose an Automatic Settings level. Start at Minimum, check your site, and move up while everything still looks right.
  4. Switch on Optimize CSS Delivery, Lazy Load Images and the Page Cache.
  5. Test with PageSpeed Insights or GTmetrix. If something looks wrong, exclude the file or plugin causing it.

Documentation

The documentation explains each setting and walks you through optimizing your site, step by step.
sections.installation:
Install from your WordPress dashboard under Plugins > Add New by searching for “JCH Optimize”. To install manually:

  1. Upload the zip file and unzip it in the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings > JCH Optimize.
  4. Choose an Automatic Settings level (Minimum to Optimum) to configure file optimization, then try the other features, such as Optimize CSS Delivery, Lazy Load Images and the Page Cache. Use the Exclude options for any files, plugins or images that don’t work well with the plugin.
sections.faq:
How does the plugin speed up my site?

It changes the HTML that WordPress sends to the browser so that the page and its resources are smaller, there are fewer requests, and what the visitor sees first loads first. With the Page Cache on, pages are also served without running WordPress for each visit. The result is a faster site for your visitors and better Core Web Vitals.

Will it break my site?

Every optimization can be switched off, and files, plugins and pages that don’t work well with an optimization can be excluded from it. Use the Mode Switcher in the admin bar to switch optimization off while you troubleshoot. JCH Optimize never changes your theme, plugin or content files.

Can I use it with another caching plugin?

Use only one page cache. Two page caches interfere with each other, and JCH Optimize’s dashboard warns you when another one is active. If you’d rather keep your current page cache, switch off JCH Optimize’s Page Cache and use its file, CSS and image optimizations alongside it.

What’s the difference between the free and Pro versions?

The free version includes page caching, combining and minifying, critical CSS, lazy loading of images and more. Pro adds AI-Assisted Optimization, real-user Core Web Vitals monitoring, WebP/AVIF and responsive images, LCP preloading, unused CSS and JavaScript reduction, font optimization, advanced caching, Cloudflare integration and ticket support. See the comparison table above, or compare plans.

Where can I get help?

Start with the Troubleshooting chapter of the documentation, or ask in the support forum. Pro subscribers can also open a private support ticket on the JCH Optimize website for bugs in the plugin and for problems it causes on their site. We don’t configure or optimize sites by hand: to have your site optimized for you, use Pro’s AI-Assisted Optimization run. See Getting Support for what support covers and what to include in a ticket.

How do I know if it’s working?

Combining CSS and JavaScript files is on by default, so the plugin starts working as soon as you activate it. If your pages look the same, that’s a good sign. To confirm, view the page source in your browser: the links to your CSS and JavaScript files are replaced by links to combined files, such as:
/wp-content/cache/jch-optimize/assets/css/63fccd8dc82e3f5da947573d8ded3bd4.css

There’s no CSS formatting after enabling the plugin

View the source of your page and open the URL of the combined CSS file in your browser. By default the combined files are static files in the /wp-content/cache/jch-optimize/assets/ folder: if the file can’t be loaded, check that this folder and its files have the same permissions as the rest of your site’s files (usually 755 for folders and 644 for files). If you set ‘Combined files delivery’ to PHP, the file is sent by WordPress itself; set it back to ‘Static css and js files’ to see if that solves it.

How do I reverse the changes JCH Optimize makes to my website?

Deactivate or uninstall the plugin. It doesn’t modify any existing file or code. It only changes the HTML before it is sent to the browser. If you still see a change after deactivating it, that’s caching: clear your WordPress, server, CDN and browser caches.

6.1.1

  • [MEDIUM] Fix Cloudflare’s whole cache being cleared each time JCH Optimize removed expired files from its cache, with Enable Cloudflare purge on. Only the pages removed from the Page Cache, including pages that used an expired combined file, are cleared at Cloudflare now, sent in batches Cloudflare accepts. Deleting pages on the Page Cache page with none that are still cached no longer clears Cloudflare’s whole cache either. [Pro Version]
  • [MEDIUM] Fix JCH Optimize Pro 6.1.0 offering 6.1.0 as an update after it was installed. 6.1.0 reported its version to the update check as 6.0.2.1. [Pro Version]
  • [MEDIUM] Fix pages showing an error page when the Sprite Generator is on and the combined CSS has background images for a sprite.
  • [MEDIUM] Fix visitors who logged in with a login form on a page of the site, such as WooCommerce’s My Account page, being kept out of the Page Cache after logging out, until the end of the Page Cache’s lifetime, with Exclude form users on. The login form is a posted form, and the cookie it set stayed after logout. It is removed when the user logs out now.
  • [MEDIUM] Logging in sets the cookie that keeps logged-in users out of the capture cache right away, so the first pages they visit after logging in on wp-login.php aren’t served from it. [Pro Version]
  • [MEDIUM] Fix pages whose URL can’t be stored in the capture cache, such as a URL with %25 or .. in its query string, showing an error page when served from the Page Cache, and stopping the Page Cache page from listing cached pages. These pages aren’t capture-cached now. [Pro Version]
  • [LOW] Fix PHP warnings and notices being shown in the responses to the plugin’s admin requests on sites that display PHP errors, which could stop the admin pages working.
  • [LOW] Fix Stripe’s script (js.stripe.com) being combined and moved with the other scripts. It is left where it is again.
  • [LOW] Fix the Exclude image from sprite and Include additional images in sprite settings failing to list the sprite’s images.
  • [LOW] Fix Add Image Attributes showing an error on pages with an image button (<input type="image">).
  • [LOW] Fix Load responsive images leaving a broken style attribute on an element above the fold with several background images in its style attribute. All of them are moved to the style element now. [Pro Version]
  • [LOW] Optimize Images adds each image to its list of optimized images once. An image optimized again was added again, so the list kept growing. [Pro Version]

6.1.0

  • Raised the minimum PHP version to 8.1.
  • Updated bundled third-party libraries to current stable releases, including Symfony DomCrawler, Guzzle and Laminas.
  • Improved cache storage by deduplicating identical optimized content, reducing cache size on disk.
  • Settings exports are now downloaded directly and no longer include the Cloudflare API token, Redis password or Download ID.
  • Importing settings keeps the site’s current Cloudflare API token, Redis password and Download ID when the file doesn’t include them.
  • Page Cache only stores pages requested on the host of the site’s home URL.
  • Redis hosts written as unix:///path, or any absolute path, are recognized as Unix sockets.
  • Uninstalling deletes the plugin’s cache folder and the next-gen and responsive images it created. Backups of optimized images are kept.
  • [HIGH] Fixed a cross-site scripting vulnerability where encoded characters in URLs, such as search query links, were decoded during optimization.
  • [HIGH] Required a valid nonce for all administrator tasks that change settings or files.
  • [HIGH] Fixed an open redirect through the return parameter of the Clean Cache task.
  • [HIGH] Validated image URLs and paths returned by the image optimization service and kept image folders within the site root.
  • [HIGH] Fixed CSS and JavaScript files outside the site root being readable through encoded slashes (..%2F) in their URLs when files are combined.
  • [HIGH] Removed the jchbackend URL parameter that disabled optimization for any visitor.
  • [MEDIUM] Page Cache no longer stores pages left unoptimized for a single request, such as pages loaded in an iframe, requested with jchnooptimize, or where optimization failed.
  • [MEDIUM] Combining files no longer fetches files from private network addresses, or follows redirects to them.
  • [MEDIUM] Page Cache’s cookies follow the COOKIEPATH and COOKIE_DOMAIN settings, are HTTPS only on HTTPS sites, and cover the whole site.
  • [MEDIUM] After an update, the .htaccess changes and the Mode Switcher must-use plugin wait for an administrator who can activate plugins, instead of running on a visitor’s request.

short_description: Faster pages, better PageSpeed scores, Core Web Vitals that pass. Page cache, critical CSS, combine & minify, lazy load. No code needed.
description:
Make your WordPress site load faster, score higher on PageSpeed Insights, and pass Core Web Vitals, without editing a line of code.

JCH Optimize optimizes each page as WordPress serves it. It combines and minifies your CSS and JavaScript, inlines the critical CSS so the page paints right away, lazy loads offscreen images, caches whole pages, and more. It targets the metrics Google measures: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), Interaction to Next Paint (INP), First Contentful Paint (FCP), Total Blocking Time (TBT) and Time to First Byte (TTFB).

It never modifies your theme, your plugins or your files. Deactivate it and your site is exactly as it was.

Why speed matters

  • Visitors stay. Slow pages lose people before they see your content. Fast pages keep them reading, browsing and buying.
  • Better search visibility. Google uses Core Web Vitals as part of its page experience ranking signals.
  • More conversions. Each second you save makes it easier for visitors to sign up, check out or get in touch.

Free features

Page caching

  • Page Cache. Serves pages from the cache without running WordPress for each visit, so the first byte arrives sooner.
  • Browser caching for cached pages, following the cache lifetime you set.
  • Campaign-friendly caching. Ignores ad and social tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, msclkid) so links from campaigns still get the cached page.
  • Leaves personal pages out. Logged-in users and visitors who just submitted a form, such as a WooCommerce cart, aren’t served cached pages.
  • Scheduled cleanup of expired cache, run by WP-Cron instead of slowing down visitors’ page loads.
  • Editors can clear the cache from Tools > Page Cache, without access to the settings.

CSS and JavaScript

  • Automatic Settings. Six levels from Minimum to Optimum set up file optimization for you. Start at Minimum and move up.
  • Combine and minify CSS, JavaScript and HTML to cut file sizes and requests.
  • Optimize CSS Delivery. Extracts the critical CSS for the top of each page, inlines it, and loads the rest without blocking rendering. This addresses PageSpeed’s render-blocking resources warning.
  • Dynamic CSS Selectors. Keeps styles for menus, sliders and other elements that JavaScript adds after the page loads in the critical CSS.
  • Defer JavaScript or move it to the bottom of the page.
  • Remove CSS and JavaScript files your pages don’t need.
  • Custom, mobile and desktop CSS, added after your combined CSS so it takes precedence.
  • Exclusions for files, plugins and pages that need to be left alone.

Images

  • Lazy load images below the first screen, so they load only when the visitor scrolls near them.
  • Add width and height attributes to images that are missing them, preventing layout shifts (CLS).
  • Sprite Generator. Combines small background images into one file.

Delivery

  • GZip compression and browser caching rules written to .htaccess for you.
  • CDN / cookieless domain support to serve static files from another domain.
  • HTTP/2 Preload for JavaScript modules and the files you choose.

Built to be safe

  • Development / Production Mode Switcher in the admin bar: switch optimization off while you work on your site, then back on, with the settings pages still available.
  • Dashboard with an optimization snapshot and notifications, including a warning when another page caching plugin is active.
  • Logs that tell you why a page wasn’t optimized or cached.

Go further with JCH Optimize Pro

The free version gets you a long way. JCH Optimize Pro adds the features that move the hardest PageSpeed metrics (LCP, unused CSS and JavaScript, image delivery), plus tools that tell you how your site performs for real visitors.

  • AI-Assisted Optimization (beta). An AI optimizes a page of your site the way an experienced person would. It tries each batch of settings on a private preview your visitors don’t see, checks in a browser for anything that broke and fixes it, and measures the result with PageSpeed Insights on mobile and desktop. It keeps the settings that made the page faster and ends with a report of the scores before and after. Needs an AI Optimization license and your own Anthropic (Claude) or OpenAI API key.
  • Page Experience (real-user monitoring). Measures LCP, INP, CLS, FCP and TTFB in your visitors’ own browsers and charts them day by day, by device and by page. Set a baseline and get an email when your site gets slower.
  • Optimize Images. Compresses images and creates WebP and AVIF versions and responsive sizes for phones and tablets, then serves them automatically. Scheduled optimization works through new images in the background, and your originals are always kept.
  • LCP image preloading. Finds the image that real visitors’ browsers report as each page’s largest paint and loads it first, on mobile and desktop.
  • Reduce unused CSS and JavaScript. Holds back CSS and scripts until the visitor interacts with the page, and loads analytics and ad scripts after the first paint, so they don’t count against your LCP or TBT.
  • Optimize Fonts. Hosts Google Fonts on your own site, preloads the fonts the top of the page needs, and adds size-matched fallback fonts so text doesn’t jump when web fonts load.
  • Advanced lazy loading for iframes, CSS background images, audio and video, plus a lightweight placeholder that stands in for YouTube embeds until clicked.
  • Reduce DOM size by loading chosen sections of the page after it renders.
  • Faster, smarter caching. Serve cached pages as static files straight from the web server, store the cache in Redis, Memcached or APCu, warm the cache with the Recache crawler, and purge the right pages automatically when you publish or update content. Other systems can purge pages through the REST API.
  • Cloudflare integration. Purges Cloudflare’s copies of your pages along with JCH Optimize’s, and switches Cloudflare’s Development Mode with the Mode Switcher.
  • Multiple CDN domains and Smart Combine bundling for HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.
  • Ticket support. Open a private support ticket for bugs in JCH Optimize and for anything it breaks on your site, such as a menu, a slider or a form, whether the settings came from an AI-assisted run or were set by hand.

Get started in minutes

  1. Install and activate JCH Optimize.
  2. While you configure it, switch off other page caching plugins.
  3. Go to Settings > JCH Optimize and choose an Automatic Settings level. Start at Minimum, check your site, and move up while everything still looks right.
  4. Switch on Optimize CSS Delivery, Lazy Load Images and the Page Cache.
  5. Test with PageSpeed Insights or GTmetrix. If something looks wrong, exclude the file or plugin causing it.

Documentation

The documentation explains each setting and walks you through optimizing your site, step by step.
